cluster_summary: The cluster predominantly consists of XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerabilities caused by using default Java XML parser configurations that permit external entity processing, DTD declarations, or external DTD loading. The majority of CVEs are due to missing explicit disabling of these features on SAX, DOM, StAX, or JAXB parsers. A few distinct members involve other XML-related issues: system property substitution, XML name validation, XMLDecoder deserialization, and removal of a vulnerable third-party library.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Remove the call to the system property resolution function from the SAML parsing code, so that attribute values and element text are returned unchanged..

mechanism.typical_fix: Remove the call to the system property resolution function from the SAML parsing code, so that attribute values and element text are returned unchanged.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Remove the call to the system property resolution function from the SAML parsing code, so that attribute values and element text are returned unchanged.
sub_patterns.name: Unsanitized system property substitution in SAML data
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled SAML attribute values and element text are passed through a function that resolves system property placeholders, allowing an attacker to exfiltrate system properties.
